transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… it’s kind of embarrassing, but at work, if I even think there might be a bat or something flapping around in the stockroom, I just… my heart jumps, I start sweating, and I feel like I have to get out right away.
Does this kind of reaction happen only when you think about bats, or does it also happen in other situations, like when you're in crowded places or feel trapped somewhere else?

Mostly bats. I don’t really get that in crowds or anything like that. It’s more like… even if I know it probably can’t hurt me, if I see something that looks like one, or just a quick flutter in the back hallway, my brain reacts like I’m in real danger.
When you feel this reaction to bats, does it lead you to avoid certain places or situations, like staying out of the stockroom or avoiding areas where you think one might be?

Yeah… I guess so. I’ve been trading away some closing shifts when I can, and I’ll take the long way around the loading area. If I have to check the stairwell, I just do it really fast, usually holding my phone, and I’m pretty scared the whole time.
Has this fear of bats caused you a lot of distress or interfered with your job or other daily activities?

Yeah… it has. My manager’s started asking if I can really handle being shift lead, because I keep swapping out of closing and I’m not as dependable with the after-hours checks. I don’t like saying it, but… it feels like it could mess up the management position I’ve been working toward.
How long have you felt this way about bats—has it been going on for several months, or longer than six months?
Longer than six months. It’s been… about two years, I think. Since that night a bat got into the back corridor during a receiving shift.
